hints.title: Canonical Slope Reduction
hints.text: Normalize direction vectors (dx, dy) by their greatest common divisor to represent slopes uniquely.

hints.title: Parallel Intercept Grouping
hints.text: Group collinear or parallel segments using their constant line offset dy * x - dx * y.

hints.title: Distinct Offset Combinatorics
hints.text: Pair segments having identical direction vector but distinct offset values.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List
from collections import defaultdict
import math

class Solution:
    def countTrapezoids(self, segments: List[List[int]]) -> int:
        # segments[i] = [x1, y1, x2, y2]
        # Group segments by canonical slope (dy, dx)
        slope_groups = defaultdict(list)
        
        for x1, y1, x2, y2 in segments:
            dx = x2 - x1
            dy = y2 - y1
            g = math.gcd(dx, dy)
            dx //= g
            dy //= g
            if dx < 0 or (dx == 0 and dy < 0):
                dx = -dx
                dy = -dy
            # Intercept representation: cross product / constant c = dy * x1 - dx * y1
            c = dy * x1 - dx * y1
            slope_groups[(dy, dx)].append(c)

        total = 0
        for slope, intercepts in slope_groups.items():
            # Segments with different intercepts can form parallel bases
            intercept_counts = defaultdict(int)
            for c in intercepts:
                intercept_counts[c] += 1
                
            running_sum = 0
            for count in intercept_counts.values():
                total += running_sum * count
                running_sum += count
                
        return total
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Pairwise collinearity tests without hash classification take O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Slope hash map bins segments by geometric orientation in linear space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Normalize slopes with GCD and count parallel pairs across distinct intercepts.
